title: Communities Lead the Fight Against Ebola in Central Africa
subtitle: As the outbreak continues in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, local involvement is becoming the key to saving lives.

summary.en: The Democratic Republic of the Congo is currently facing its deadliest Ebola outbreak ever recorded. With over 2,500 deaths, health officials are shifting their strategy to focus on local community leadership. Experts emphasize that local people understand their own neighborhoods best and can help stop the spread of the virus. While international aid and military conflict remain significant challenges, success in neighboring Uganda shows that the virus can be contained. The response now relies on working directly with villages to identify and isolate cases early.
summary.zh: 剛果民主共和國目前正面臨史上最致命的伊波拉疫情。隨著死亡人數超過兩千五百人，衛生官員正調整策略，將重心轉向由地方社區主導。專家強調，當地民眾最了解自己的社區，能協助遏止病毒傳播。儘管國際援助與軍事衝突仍是重大挑戰，但鄰國烏干達的成功經驗顯示，該病毒是可以被控制的。目前的防疫工作仰賴與村莊直接合作，以利及早發現並隔離病例。

paragraphs.en: The Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has reached a difficult milestone in its fight against the Ebola virus. One hundred days after the government declared the 17th outbreak of the disease, it has become the deadliest in the country's history. According to The Guardian Health, the outbreak has resulted in approximately 2,500 deaths. Behind these numbers are families facing not only the fear of a deadly disease but also the challenges of conflict and limited access to medical care.
paragraphs.zh: 剛果民主共和國 (DRC) 在對抗伊波拉病毒的戰役中，來到了一個艱難的里程碑。在政府宣布該國爆發第十七次疫情的一百天後，這場疫情已成為該國歷史上最致命的一次。根據衛報健康版報導，這場疫情已導致約兩千五百人死亡。在這些數字背後，是無數家庭不僅要面對致命疾病的恐懼，還要承受戰亂與醫療資源匱乏的挑戰。

paragraphs.en: Ebola is a serious virus that spreads through contact with infected bodily fluids. In the current crisis, health workers are dealing with the Bundibugyo strain, a rare type of the virus. KFF Health News reports that this specific strain has a 44% fatality rate, meaning nearly half of those who catch it do not survive. Furthermore, the medical response is made much harder by military conflict in the eastern part of the country, which makes it difficult for doctors and supplies to reach the people who need them most.
paragraphs.zh: 伊波拉是一種透過接觸受感染體液傳播的嚴重病毒。在當前的危機中，醫護人員正在應對一種罕見的病毒株——邦迪布焦病毒株。凱澤家庭基金會健康新聞 (KFF Health News) 指出，這種特定病毒株的致死率高達百分之四十四，意味著近半數感染者無法存活。此外，該國東部的軍事衝突使醫療應對工作變得更加困難，導致醫師與物資難以送達最需要的人手中。

paragraphs.en: Despite these obstacles, there is hope. Uganda recently declared the end of its own Ebola outbreak, proving that the virus can be stopped when national leaders and local communities work together. According to The Guardian Health, the secret to this success is simple: involving the people who live in the affected areas. When health workers first arrived in the DRC, they realized that they needed to listen to the people they were trying to help. Community members, including survivors, women, and local leaders, know exactly where families go for help and why some people might be afraid of medical teams.
paragraphs.zh: 儘管困難重重，仍有一線希望。烏干達近期宣布該國的伊波拉疫情結束，證明了當國家領導人與地方社區攜手合作時，病毒是可以被遏止的。根據衛報健康版報導，成功的秘訣很簡單：讓受影響地區的居民參與其中。當醫護人員最初抵達剛果民主共和國時，他們意識到必須傾聽那些他們試圖幫助的人們。社區成員，包括倖存者、婦女與地方領袖，最清楚家庭會去哪裡尋求協助，也了解為何有些人會對醫療團隊感到恐懼。

paragraphs.en: This "village-centred" strategy is now the main focus of the response. Instead of just sending outsiders to manage the situation, health organizations are working to empower local people. These community members can help identify illness early, share accurate information to stop dangerous rumors, and support families during the difficult process of treatment. As noted by The Guardian Health, the response moves much faster when communities lead alongside national authorities and professional health workers.
paragraphs.zh: 這種「以村莊為中心」的策略，現在已成為防疫工作的核心重點。醫療組織不再只是派遣外來人員來處理狀況，而是致力於賦權當地民眾。這些社區成員能協助及早發現病患、分享正確資訊以遏止危險的謠言，並在艱難的治療過程中支持家庭。正如衛報健康版所指出的，當社區與國家當局及專業醫護人員並肩領導時，防疫工作的進展會快得多。

paragraphs.en: International organizations are also playing a vital role. The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) has joined forces with other global health groups to create a unified plan. KFF Health News reports that these groups are working to improve cross-border communication and provide better training for local staff. They are also using advanced tools like genomic surveillance—the study of the virus’s genetic code—to track how the disease is changing and spreading.
paragraphs.zh: 國際組織也扮演著至關重要的角色。非洲疾病管制暨預防中心 (Africa CDC) 已與其他全球衛生團體聯手，制定了一項統一的計畫。凱澤家庭基金會健康新聞報導稱，這些團體正致力於改善跨境溝通，並為當地工作人員提供更好的培訓。他們也正運用基因監測等先進工具——即研究病毒的基因密碼——來追蹤病毒如何變異與傳播。

paragraphs.en: However, the work is far from over. The emergency continues, and cases are still being found outside of known contact lists. Every time a new case appears that was not expected, it means the virus has had another chance to spread. Experts warn that every delay gives the virus an advantage. To stop the transmission, teams must reach the most remote villages, provide reliable equipment, and ensure that health workers are paid and protected.
paragraphs.zh: 然而，工作遠未結束。緊急狀態仍在持續，且在已知的接觸者名單之外，仍不斷發現新的病例。每一次出現意料之外的新病例，都意味著病毒又有機會進一步擴散。專家警告，任何耽擱都會讓病毒佔據優勢。為了阻斷傳播，團隊必須深入最偏遠的村莊，提供可靠的設備，並確保醫護人員獲得薪資與保護。

paragraphs.en: Erica Tavares, a senior director at the International Medical Corps, told KFF Health News that the global community was behind in its response when the outbreak first began. Now, the goal is to make up for that lost time. The U.S. government has pledged $512 million in aid to help with the response, but money alone is not enough. The success of the current efforts depends on building trust in areas where fear and misinformation have taken hold.
paragraphs.zh: 國際醫療隊 (International Medical Corps) 資深總監艾莉卡·塔瓦雷斯 (Erica Tavares) 向凱澤家庭基金會健康新聞表示，當疫情剛開始時，全球社群的反應慢了一步。現在，目標是彌補失去的時間。美國政府已承諾提供五億一千兩百萬美元的援助以協助防疫，但僅靠金錢是不夠的。當前努力的成功，取決於在恐懼與錯誤資訊根深蒂固的地區建立信任。

paragraphs.en: As the response enters this new phase, the focus remains on the people on the ground. From laboratory teams identifying the virus to burial teams helping families honor their loved ones with dignity, the work is dangerous and exhausting. Many health workers have even contracted the disease themselves while trying to save others. Their safety and support are now considered central to the entire mission. By combining international resources with the deep knowledge of local communities, health officials hope to finally break the chains of transmission and bring an end to this deadly outbreak.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著防疫工作進入新階段，重點依然放在第一線的人員身上。從鑑定病毒的實驗室團隊，到協助家庭以尊嚴方式送別摯愛的喪葬團隊，這項工作既危險又令人精疲力竭。許多醫護人員在試圖拯救他人時，甚至自己也感染了疾病。他們的安全與後勤支援，現在被視為整個任務的核心。透過結合國際資源與當地社區的深厚知識，衛生官員希望能最終切斷傳播鏈，終結這場致命的疫情。

keyTerms.definitionEn: Late or slower than expected in progress or development.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作介系詞（在...後面），這裡作形容詞表示進度落後。文中：Erica Tavares, a senior director at the International Medical Corps, told KFF Health News that the global community was behind in its response when the outbreak first began.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To become established or have a strong influence.
keyTerms.definitionZh: （觀念、恐懼等）紮根、確立、產生強大影響。
keyTerms.noteZh: 這是一個慣用語，指某種情緒或現象變得根深蒂固。文中：The success of the current efforts depends on building trust in areas where fear and misinformation have taken hold.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To work together with someone else to achieve a common goal.
keyTerms.noteZh: 字面意思是「加入武力」，實際是指團體間的合作。文中：The Africa Centres for Disease Control and Prevention (Africa CDC) has joined forces with other global health groups to create a unified plan.

keyTerms.definitionEn: In the actual location where an event or activity is happening, rather than from a remote office.
keyTerms.noteZh: 指在實際發生事件的地點工作，而非遠端指揮。文中：As the response enters this new phase, the focus remains on the people on the ground.

quiz.question: What is the primary reason the fatality rate of the current Ebola outbreak in the DRC is significant?

options.A: It is the first time the Bundibugyo strain has ever been identified in the country.
options.B: The current strain has a 44% fatality rate, meaning nearly half of those infected die.
options.C: It is the most expensive outbreak to treat in the history of the DRC.
options.D: The military conflict has caused the fatality rate to rise to over 90%.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。根據文章第二段，文中明確指出目前的疫情是 Bundibugyo 病毒株，其致死率為 44%，即近半數感染者無法存活。選項 A 錯誤，文章僅提到這是罕見病毒株，未說是首次發現；選項 C 錯誤，文中未提到治療成本的歷史比較；選項 D 錯誤，文中提到衝突使醫療反應變困難，但並未指出致死率因此上升至 90%。

quiz.question: Based on the text, why did initial international efforts to contain the Ebola outbreak struggle to succeed?

options.A: They focused too much on genomic surveillance instead of providing medical supplies.
options.B: They lacked the financial support from the U.S. government at the beginning.
options.C: They failed to incorporate local knowledge and community trust into their strategy.
options.D: They were unable to find enough health workers willing to enter the eastern part of the country.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據文章第三與第四段，初期反應者多為「外來者」，後來發現必須傾聽當地人意見並建立信任。文章暗示初期策略缺乏這種在地連結，導致進展緩慢。選項 A 錯誤，基因監測是後來才加入的工具；選項 B 錯誤，文中提到錢不是唯一問題；選項 D 錯誤，文中雖提到工作危險，但並未指出缺乏人力是初期失敗的主因。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, what does the phrase 'break the chains of transmission' mean in context?

options.A: To physically dismantle the medical equipment used for treatment.
options.B: To stop the virus from spreading from one person to another.
options.C: To end the military conflict that is hindering medical teams.
options.D: To force local communities to follow strict quarantine rules.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。在流行病學背景下，「break the chains of transmission」意指切斷病毒在人與人之間的傳播途徑，使疫情停止擴散。選項 A 錯誤，這與醫療器材無關；選項 C 錯誤，雖然衝突是阻礙，但這句話專指病毒傳播；選項 D 錯誤，這句話描述的是防疫目標，而非強制手段。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article regarding the fight against Ebola in the DRC?

options.A: The Ebola virus is becoming impossible to control due to constant genetic mutations.
options.B: Financial aid from international governments is the only way to end the outbreak.
options.C: Military intervention is required to secure medical supply lines in remote areas.
options.D: Effective response requires combining international resources with local community engagement.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 D。全文的核心論點在於，單靠外來資源或資金不足以解決疫情，必須結合國際組織的專業（如基因監測、資金）與在地化的策略（如傾聽當地人、建立信任），才能有效控制疫情。選項 A 錯誤，文章提到有希望控制；選項 B 錯誤，文中強調錢不是萬能的；選項 C 錯誤，文中提到軍事衝突是困難點，但未主張以軍事介入解決問題。
